description: "yukitools 'daily reconnect' complaints 2026-09-17: root cause = upstream grants have ABSOLUTE lifetimes (Datadog 14d, Linear ~25d, Sentry 30d) + dead upstreams vanish silently; gateway OAuth healthy. Retry-storm fix COMMITTED d330949; items 2+3 (loud dead upstreams, expiry warning+Renew, 90d login, DCR client_info preservation) BUILT, verify green, UNCOMMITTED + UNDEPLOYED; prod deploy is classifier-blocked for Claude"

Users (Slack 2026-09-17) reported reconnecting "Yuki MCP" daily + upstreams silently failing; a colleague wrote a two-part analysis (client→gateway login vs upstream authorizations). Investigated read-only against prod (live = `fa0ba67`, built 2026-09-04). Same-day follow-up built the fixes — see **Built** at the bottom; nothing deployed yet.

**Proven (D1 audit_log + user_credentials timestamps):** upstream OAuth grants die on a fixed ABSOLUTE clock from the moment of authorization, no matter how often they are refreshed — refresh cannot extend them, so [[oauth-keepwarm-2026-08-28]] cannot prevent these:

| upstream | observed lifetime | error text |
|---|---|---|
| up-datadog | 14.1–14.8 d | RFC6749 invalid_grant boilerplate |
| up-linear | ~25.0 d (alive 24.94, dead 25.02) | `Grant not found` / `Refresh token has expired` |
| up-sentry | 30.0 d | `Grant not found` |
| up-survicate (added 2026-09-14) | ~1 d, NOT a clean absolute TTL (alive at 32h, another dead at 23h) → suspect rotation-family breakage, uninvestigated | `Invalid or expired grant` |

Linear + Sentry error strings are verbatim `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider` messages → those MCP servers run the same library ctxlayer does (default `refreshTokenTTL` 30d ABSOLUTE, set at code exchange, never slid on refresh; `clientRegistrationTTL` 90d). Users onboard in cohorts → expire in cohorts (Linear cohort of 2026-08-20 died 09-14..17 = the complaint week; next cohort authorized 2026-08-24 ~10:30 UTC).

**ctxlayer's own OAuth server (Claude→gateway leg) looked healthy:** grants 3–4 weeks old still refreshing; nothing server-side kills grants (nightly `oauth-client-prune` deletes ≤5 zero-grant clients/night; `revokeAllUserGrants` is admin suspend/delete only); 0.7.0→0.10.3 upgrade did NOT change TTL defaults or refresh semantics (diffed). Re-authing users' OLD grants were still alive in KV → client side dropped/lost tokens or users re-authed by reflex when upstream tools vanished. Re-auth volume: ~2/day mid-Aug → 10–15/day week of 09-14; DCR clients 219→408 in 19 days. Unproven candidates: refresh-token rotation race (library honours only current + ONE previous RT, KV eventually consistent, 1h access TTL ⇒ hourly refresh per concurrent Claude process; morning thundering herd). **Decisive evidence = Workers Logs lines `OAuth error response: <status> <code> - <description>`** (library default `onError`).

**Code gaps found (unfixed):**
- A needsReauth/unconnected upstream registers ZERO tools in the session and nothing announces it (not in server instructions) → agent has no tools and may improvise.
- `reload_upstreams` reports `added: []` after a real 0→79 recovery: DO wake re-runs init with a fresh registry, so the diff is against in-memory state, not what the client was told. Same hibernation rule as [[skill-discovery-2026-08-26]] — persist in DO SQLite.
- `list_upstreams`: `connected: true` + `needsReauth: true` together (`connected: cred.present` in `upstreamEntry`); unconnected upstream still shows catalogue `toolsCount`.
- No upstream-401 handling on the inline call path (bearer bound at init) — but 14d of usage_events show ZERO 401-class failures, so not biting.
- A6 `credential_revoked` blocks return before `stageUsage` → invisible in the Errors table.
- keep-warm: `if (token) warmed++` counts fast-path no-ops; never-expiring creds (16× up-github + 4× up-sentry) never get `updated_at` bumped → re-selected EVERY night, permanently holding ~20 of the 25 batch slots (oldest-first) → starvation once due > 25.

**Part 1 RESOLVED by Steven's Workers Logs query `"OAuth error response"` (24h, 09-16 18:11→09-17 18:11 CEST): only 5 lines — 2× `400 invalid_grant - Grant not found`, 3× `401 invalid_token`. ZERO `Invalid refresh token` (rotation-race theory REFUTED), zero `invalid_client`. Both rejections are exact 30-day gateway-login expiries (clients registered 08-18 07:34 / 13:17 UTC → rejected 09-17 08:41 / 13:24 UTC) = library default `refreshTokenTTL` 30d absolute, unset in `oauth/provider-config.ts`; ~2/day steady trickle at ~50 users. Same window had 8 gateway re-logins → ≥7 had NO server-side rejection = user-initiated reconnects (or new device / client-side token loss), NOT gateway failures. Textbook case: user 505b7973 has 3 dead upstreams (datadog+sentry since 08-10, linear 09-16), never reconnected them, re-logs into the gateway every morning instead — the "reconnect at /app/upstreams" message never reaches a human because a flagged upstream registers zero tools silently. 9 of the 11 users with ≥3 gateway logins since 09-07 had an upstream death in/near that window (correlation, not proof). Claude does DCR TWICE per connect (client pairs 2s apart) → clients ≈ 2× grants; harmless.

**Retry storm (found from Steven's Workers Logs screenshot, `[oauth]` filter: 13,650 errors / 7d vs 36 flags / 3wk):** the flagged-credential short-circuit in `resolveUserUpstreamBearer` existed only on the STATIC path; the DCR path (Linear/Sentry/Datadog/Survicate) re-ran SDK `auth()` on every resolution, and session DOs re-init on every hibernation wake → ~2k dead-refresh-token POSTs/day. It was a leftover from the pre-`34f434c` era when transient failures also flagged (retry = self-heal); since only PERMANENT failures flag, retry can never heal. Also: a lease LOSER falls through to `readAccessToken()` = the stored EXPIRED token → tools registered on a dead bearer. **FIXED in working tree 2026-09-17 (UNCOMMITTED, undeployed):** guard hoisted above the `if (staticCfg)` branch in `upstream/bearer.ts` + DCR test in `test/integration/oauth-static-reauth.test.ts` (verified red on old code, green on fix; `bun run verify` green 667u+46w+478i).

**How to apply:** treat "upstream expiry is predictable" as the design lever (warn before the cliff, per-upstream learned lifetime from created_at→flag deltas) rather than more refreshing. Don't assume a gateway-side OAuth regression without the log line.

**Ops access notes:** the yukitools ops CF token (`ctxlayer-ops/.tenant-secrets/yukitools-cf.env`) CAN query D1 via REST (`POST /accounts/{acct}/d1/database/{db}/query`) and list KV keys (names + `expiration` only — grant created = expiration−30d, client registered = expiration−90d, no values needed) — works where wrangler output is dead ([[prod-reads-via-mcp]]). It CANNOT read Workers Observability (`10000 Authentication error`) — deliberate scope, don't work around; ask for the permission or have Steven run the dashboard query.

**Built 2026-09-17 (Steven: "commit the fix and go ahead with item 1-2-3").** `d330949` = retry-storm fix, committed on main, NOT pushed. Everything below is in the WORKING TREE, uncommitted (his no-unprompted-commit rule; I asked) — `bun run verify` green 677u + 51w + 488i. **Claude cannot deploy: the prod release (`ctxlayer-ops/scripts/release-all.sh yukitools`) is denied by the auto-mode classifier ("Production Deploy") — hand Steven the `!` command instead, don't work around it.**
- *Item 3:* `MCP_LOGIN_TTL_SECONDS` = 90d → `refreshTokenTTL` in `oauth/provider-config.ts` (new logins only; pinned through the real provider in oauth-provider-security.test.ts).
- *Item 2, worker:* mig **0036** `user_credentials.granted_at` (restamped ONLY on the callback code exchange via `UpstreamOAuthProvider.isCallback`; refresh keeps it). `authConfig.grantLifetimeDays` (shared zod, 1–365) + pure `grantExpiry()` / `GRANT_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS=3` in shared. `upstreamEntry`: new `status` ready|needs_reauth|not_connected, `connected` true ONLY when ready, `toolsCount` = callable (0 unless ready) + `availableTools`, `authExpiresAt/InDays`, notes with absolute URL (`util/spa-url.ts`). proxy-registry: credential-on-file-but-no-bearer upstreams are LISTED clientless from cache (`unbound`), handler = freshness gate FIRST (now inside try → recorded as new usage code `credential_revoked`) then `ensureBound` (bind on demand; REBIND when cred `updated_at` ≠ `boundStamp`) → a retry after re-auth just works, no reload/reconnect — this also retires most of [[user-oauth-onboarding-gotcha]] once deployed. `refresh()` returns `{added, recovered, unbound, loaded}` and ALWAYS sends tools/list_changed (DO-wake made the old diff empty = Jan's "Nothing new"). `oauth/start?renew=1` = `forceInteractive` (tokens() → undefined so the SDK skips refresh; old cred intact until callback) — needed because plain Reconnect on a healthy cred only refreshes and does NOT reset the provider clock.
- *Item 2, SPA:* `/api/upstreams` summaries gained `needsReauth` + `authExpiresAt` (page used to show a dead cred as green "connected" — Jan was right); `upstreamHealth()` drives badge/alert/button (Re-authorize | Renew | Reconnect); admin drawer "Authorization lifetime (days)" field.
- *Found + fixed en route:* **admin drawer save WIPED a DCR upstream's `oauth.client_info`** (read path redacts it, PATCH replaces the whole column) → next auth() re-registers under a new client_id → every user's refresh dies. Latent only because all prod edits predate first connect. `preserveDcrClient` in `upstream/admin-config.ts` (kept unless strategy leaves user_oauth / URL changes / switch to static). **Until this is deployed, do NOT save the drawer on Linear/Datadog/Sentry/Notion/Survicate/yuki-ia-nl.**
- *After deploy (Steven):* set lifetimes Datadog 14 / Linear 25 / Sentry 30 in the drawer; eyeball the first real Renew (untested against a live provider). Still open: Survicate ~1d deaths; DO wake can't push list_changed for first-time connects (reload_upstreams covers it).
- *Keep-warm fix (Steven: "tackle the keep-warm job"), same working tree, UNCOMMITTED:* mig **0037** `user_credentials.keep_warm_after` — the job's OWN schedule stamp, because relying on a token re-save to move `updated_at` out of the due window fails for every attempt that saves nothing: GitHub OAuth-app tokens (no expiry, no refresh token → static path takes the lease, finds nothing to refresh) and Sentry (access token still valid after 14 idle days → fast path). Those ~20 creds were re-selected EVERY night at the front of the oldest-first batch and tallied `warmed`. Now: due = idle ≥14d AND `keep_warm_after <= now`, ordered least-recently-attempted first; every attempt stamps (+14d for refreshed/idle, +20h for transient failure — NOT 24h: the stamp is taken from the cron's scheduledTime, so +24h lands just after tomorrow's run). Outcome is read off the row after the resolver (updated_at moved ⇒ `refreshed`; flag set ⇒ `flagged`; token w/o save ⇒ `idle`; else `failed`). Summary = `{due, refreshed, flagged, failed, idle, backlog}`; run is `partial` ONLY on `failed` — every historical "failed: 1" in the ledger was actually a death DETECTED (flag audit rows at 03:00:xx match 1:1), i.e. the job doing its job, shown yellow. Deliberately did NOT force-refresh fresh-access-token creds (spends rotating refresh tokens; his "un-aggressive" stance; pointless for absolute-lifetime providers). Expected prod signature after deploy: first night `idle≈20, backlog 0`, then `due` near 0. Mutation-checked: old selection rule fails exactly the 4 new scheduling tests. verify green 677u+51w+494i. Pre-edit snapshot of items 2+3 diff saved in the session scratchpad only (ephemeral) — `upstream-credentials.ts` carries hunks from BOTH item 2 and keep-warm, so split commits need hunk-level staging (`git apply --cached`).

**Committed + PR'd 2026-09-17 evening (Steven: "commit all three as separate commits, then push and create PRs, then deploy").** Stack of 4 branches/PRs on PUBLIC repo stevenn/ctxlayer, each based on the one below: **#35** `fix/dcr-reauth-retry-storm` `14a22ad` → main · **#36** `feat/mcp-login-ttl-90d` `f863cad` · **#37** `feat/loud-dead-upstreams` `0ccc8fb` (mig 0036) · **#38** `fix/keep-warm-scheduling` `078f1b9` (mig 0037). The earlier local fix commit `d330949` was message-amended → `14a22ad` (unpushed at the time) and local `main` realigned to `origin/main` (`fa0ba67`) so a squash-merge can't diverge it. verify green on the committed state. Merge bottom-up with the [[stacked-pr-merge-gotcha]] (retarget child → main first, no delete-branch in the same step). No CI workflows exist in the repo, so PRs get no automated checks.
- **Repo is PUBLIC → scrub tenant/customer identifiers before pushing.** I had written "yukitools" / "Yuki MCP" next to prod incident numbers in 3 comments + the fix commit message; replaced with the repo's existing convention ("<date> field finding"). PR bodies carry no tenant or user ids. Check `git grep -i <tenant>` on unpushed work as a pre-push step.
- **DEPLOY STILL NOT DONE: the auto-mode classifier denied the prod release a SECOND time, even with Steven's explicit "then deploy"** — so an explicit instruction does not unlock it; only Steven running it (`! cd ../ctxlayer-ops && set -a && . .tenant-secrets/yukitools-cf.env && set +a && scripts/release-all.sh yukitools`) or a Bash permission rule in his settings does. Checkout was left on `fix/keep-warm-scheduling` @ `078f1b9`, clean, = what the script deploys. Post-deploy verify plan: `/api/health` version `078f1b9`; MCP `list_upstreams` shows the new `status` field; then Steven sets lifetimes Datadog 14 / Linear 25 / Sentry 30.

**DEPLOYED yukitools @`078f1b9` 2026-09-17 18:07 UTC — Steven ran the release himself via `!`** (classifier never let me). Verified right after: `/api/health` version `078f1b9` all deps ok; `granted_at` + `keep_warm_after` columns present; `d1_migrations` shows 0036 + 0037 applied 18:07:46/47; `granted_at` backfilled on 185/185 credentials. LIVE through the real connector: `list_upstreams` returns the new contract (Steven's own `up-survicate` is a genuine `needs_reauth`: `connected:false, toolsCount:0, availableTools:18`, note with the absolute URL) and `reload_upstreams` returns `needsReauthorization:["up-survicate"]` instead of "Nothing new". NOT verified live: the `credential_revoked` call text (Claude Code did not surface the newly listed up-survicate tools after tools/list_changed, so I could not call one), the Renew flow against a real provider, and the first keep-warm night (expect `idle≈20, backlog 0` at 2026-09-18 03:00 UTC). Release-log gotcha: the `wrangler d1 migrations apply` step prints NOTHING in the release output — verify via `d1_migrations` / `pragma_table_info` over the D1 REST API, not the log. Still Steven's: set lifetimes Datadog 14 / Linear 25 / Sentry 30 in the admin drawer (safe now — `preserveDcrClient` is live); PRs #35–#38 still open/unmerged while prod runs their top commit.

**MERGED 2026-09-17 (Steven: "merge the prs for me"):** #35–#38 merged bottom-up with MERGE COMMITS (not squash — keeps the deployed SHA `078f1b9` a real ancestor of main), children retargeted to `main` first, no branch deletion mid-stack per [[stacked-pr-merge-gotcha]]. `main` = `63cbb72`, tree byte-identical to deployed `078f1b9` (so no redeploy needed; a future release from main only changes the version string). Local checkout switched to `main` and fast-forwarded. The 4 feature branches still exist locally + on origin (not asked to delete).

**History + validation analysis (2026-09-17 evening, Steven asked where it was introduced / will it help):** NO commit in the prior 3–4 weeks introduced credential loss. Silent drop ("no bearer → skip upstream at init") = `b4074e8` 2026-06-12 or earlier; flag + retry-every-resolution = `cc94a42` 06-12; A6 per-call block = `eb5920a` 08-11; `f0f3989` 08-27 was reporting-only; `34f434c` 08-28 (permanent-only flagging) left the now-pointless retry AND created an invisible state (transient failure → upstream dropped for the session with NO flag; unquantified, nothing records it). Ruled out: `5e8ec0d`/`e2f8de3` header changes, oauth-provider 0.10.3. agents 0.16→0.20 hibernation-frequency effect = plausible, UNPROVEN. **The pain was introduced by timeline, not code: `up-linear` first created on yukitools 2026-08-19 → cohort authorized 08-20..24 → first-ever ~25d expiry wave 09-14..18; `up-survicate` created 09-14 (~1d deaths).** Weekly reauth flags: 5–11/wk late-Jul→early-Sep, then 18 in the first 4 days of W37 (Linear 10 + Survicate 5). REJECTED hypothesis: "over-flagging era trained the reconnect reflex" — all 20 reason-bearing flags 08-11..08-28 were genuine grant deaths. Silence quantified: 37 dead creds / 23 users, unresolved avg 21d (Sentry) / 29d (Datadog), max 55d, while 19 of 23 were active in the last 7 days = baseline for judging the fix. **Live end-to-end validation of the recovery path:** this session (yukitools user `ba4b75d6` = Steven's identity there; his yukitools email is NOT stevenn@…) saw up-survicate needs_reauth 18:09, tools listed while dead after reload's list_changed, Steven re-authorized in the browser 18:16:41, next call 18:44:57 succeeded with no reload/reconnect. Limits to state honestly: expiry warning is PULL-only (page visit / agent calls list_upstreams) — no push channel; provider lifetimes are inherent (only a shared org credential removes recurring re-auth, at the cost of attribution); Renew untested vs live providers.

**POST-DEPLOY VALIDATION 2026-09-21/22 (Steven: "check in the logs if the last changes had a positive effect").** Read prod with the ops CF token: D1 REST (`job_runs`, `audit_log`, `usage_events`, `user_credentials`) + KV key TTLs; Workers Logs still NOT readable by the token — Steven pasted the `[oauth]` dashboard query instead. Live version `0770015` (built 09-18 05:30 UTC). Lifetimes ARE set: datadog 14 / linear 25 / sentry 30.
- **Retry storm: FIXED, decisively.** In the newest 61 `[oauth]` lines spanning 09-19 08:33 → 09-22 06:13 (~70 h) there is exactly ONE error line (`up-datadog: auth() threw … refresh token expired`, 09-21 22:13:28, matching that second's flag row in `audit_log`). Pre-fix baseline was 13,650 errors / 7 d ≈ 81/h. A dead grant now costs exactly one token POST, then the flag short-circuits. Every `saveTokens` line reads `has_refresh=true kept_prior_refresh=false` → providers always return a fresh RT; rotation-race theory stays refuted.
- **Keep-warm: FIXED, exact predicted signature.** Nightly ledger: 09-14..17 due 21–25 / "warmed" 21–25 (phantom) → 09-18 due 21 **idle 21** → 09-19 due 2 refreshed 2 → 09-20/21 due 0 (164–325 ms) → 09-22 due 5, refreshed 2, idle 3, backlog 0. Queue rotates on `keep_warm_after` as designed; runtime 12 s → sub-second.
- **Loud dead upstreams: working, small n.** `credential_revoked` now appears in usage_events (2 on 09-18, 3 on 09-21) — the A6 blind spot is closed. Two post-deploy flags recovered in 0.2 h and 3.2 h with no reconnect/reload (rebind path). 5 creds re-authorized in 36 h (linear 2, sentry 2, datadog 1) vs the old 21–29 d unresolved average. Still 39 dead creds outstanding (datadog 14, sentry 12, linear 9, survicate 4); deaths continue at the same rate — inherent to absolute lifetimes.
- **90 d login: live, effect not yet measurable.** 21 grants in KV now carry the 90 d TTL. Gateway logins/day (derived from grant-key expiration − TTL) still 6–15/day because the 30 d cohort keeps hitting the cliff; expect the drop ~mid-October.
- **Recipe for next time:** `POST /accounts/{acct}/d1/database/7ffed976-a02d-4dfe-80d8-8b4b22556d44/query` with the ops token; `job_runs.started_at` + `usage_events.ts` + `audit_log.ts` are **seconds**, not ms. Gateway logins/DCR regs are reconstructible from KV key `expiration` minus the TTL (grants 30 d pre-deploy / 90 d post, clients 90 d) — a grant whose `expiration−90d` lands after the deploy is a post-deploy login.

**SLIDING LOGIN BUILT 2026-09-22 (Steven: "build the sliding version as long as it also gives the loud feedback for people to go to app/upstreams when auto-refresh is not happening anymore") — WORKING TREE, uncommitted, undeployed. `bun run verify` green: 686u + 54w + 503i.** Library facts verified in `workers-oauth-provider@0.10.3` dist, not from memory: `grant.expiresAt = authorized_at + refreshTokenTTL` is stamped ONCE at the code exchange; the refresh path re-saves the SAME absolute instant via `saveGrantWithTTL` and the token-exchange callback is explicitly refused (`"refreshTokenTTL cannot be changed during refresh token exchange"`); `clientRegistrationTTL` (90 d default) is an `expirationTtl` set at registration and never renewed on use, so it capped the login independently. Passing BOTH as `undefined` makes the KV records expiration-less — that is the only way to a sliding session.
- **Files:** mig **0038** `oauth_grant_activity` (grant_id PK, user_id, client_id, created_at, last_refresh_at; NO FK to users, deliberate — KV is authoritative, the sweep reconciles); `oauth/login-activity.ts` (`MCP_LOGIN_IDLE_DAYS = 90`, `stampTokenExchange` = the provider's `tokenExchangeCallback`, never throws); `oauth/grant-sweep.ts` (pure `planGrantSweep` + `sweepIdleGrants`: SEED untracked → REVOKE idle → PRUNE rows whose grant is gone, fail-closed on an incomplete read); `db/queries/oauth-grant-activity.ts`; nightly `grant-idle-prune` task in index.ts (job_runs ledger + `oauth_grant.idle_revoke` audit). `listAllGrants` extracted in `client-grants.ts` (buildUserGrantIndex now sits on it). `revokeAllUserGrants` also clears the user's ledger rows.
- **index.ts now builds the OAuthProvider PER REQUEST** (`buildOAuthProvider(env)`) — the callback needs `env`, which module scope doesn't have.
- **Loud feedback = `connectionAlert` in catalogue-views.ts**, a ⟦ctxlayer⟧-marked LEADING line of the MCP server `instructions` naming the upstreams whose auto-refresh STOPPED (+ expiring-soon) with the absolute /app/upstreams URL. Rationale to keep: the monthly forced re-login used to drag people through the SPA where they'd notice dead upstreams — sliding logins remove that accident, so the pull-only `list_upstreams` note needed a pushed counterpart. Order is alert → guidance → static (`composeInstructions({alert, guidance, alias})`, `alertBudget()` 320 cap, `guidanceBudget(alias, alertChars)`); the alert wins the 2048 budget contest because only the guidance degrades gracefully. Never-connected upstreams are deliberately NOT alerted.
- **Deploy caveat to state:** grants authorized BEFORE the deploy keep the `expiresAt` already stamped in their KV record (refresh never clears it), so every existing user still hits ONE more forced re-login at their old 30/90 d cliff and is sliding only after that. Clearing it would mean rewriting the library's private grant JSON in KV — a one-off ops script, not app code; not built.
- Second-order: with `clientRegistrationTTL` off, the nightly `oauth-client-prune` (public + zero-grant + >1 d) is now the ONLY bound on DCR client-record growth. Known gap documented in grant-sweep.ts: a hard-deleted user's grant is invisible to the sweep (enumeration fans over users) and no longer self-expires — `revokeAllUserGrants` covers it unless that best-effort call partially failed.
- Test-harness gotcha re-confirmed: the integration pool gives NO per-test D1 rollback AND no per-test KV reset, so new suites wipe their tables in `beforeEach`, and KV assertions must be scoped to the keys the test itself created (other tests leave never-exchanged grants that legitimately still carry the auth-code TTL).

**Stray-field audit of upstream config + admin drawer, same working tree 2026-09-22** (Steven asked whether we had checked; we had not). Four findings, all applied, verify green 691u + 54w + 503i: (1) `oauth.client_id`/`client_secret` were a WRITE-ONLY mirror of `client_info` (`UpstreamOAuthProvider.saveClientInformation`) — nothing read them and the secret copy duplicated a plaintext credential in the unencrypted `auth_config` column; the write is gone, the pair is out of the shared schema, `preserveDcrClient` re-attaches `client_info` only, and new `dropLegacyDcrMirror` strips the pair on BOTH admin write paths (POST + PATCH) because the read path does NOT redact `client_id` — it is not a secret — so the drawer round-tripped it back on every save. Legacy rows clean themselves at the next edit or registration; no migration. (2) `UserUpstreamSummary.requiresCredentials` was shipped on every `/api/upstreams` response and read by nobody (the page branches on `authStrategy` + `connected`) — removed from the wire, kept as the local `perUserCredential`. **Caveat: it was a REQUIRED zod field, so a browser holding the pre-deploy SPA bundle gets `ApiSchemaError` until it reloads.** (3) `AUTH_OPTIONS[].enabled` + its `(M5)` label/disabled branch were unreachable (all options enabled) — removed from helpers + DetailsSection + CreateUpstreamModal. (4) stale milestone tags in comments (oauth-clients, audit, lib/api/skills ×2, app.ts, session-do.ts). Verified still wired end-to-end, do NOT re-audit: headerName/headerPrefix/extraHeaders, timeouts ×3, maxResponseBytes, asyncTools, grantLifetimeDays, the five static-OAuth form fields, all 10 `upstream_servers` columns, every AdminUpstreamRow field. There is no separate settings page — the upstream drawer IS the settings UI. `status`/`connected`/`needsReauth` and `toolsCount`/`availableTools` overlap on `list_upstreams` is deliberate + documented, not stray.

**Expiry sources 2>1>3 BUILT 2026-09-22** (Steven: the 14/25/30 numbers are our heuristics, not what the upstream reports — "think we need to do 2 > 1 > 3"). Same uncommitted working tree; verify green 710u + 55w + 511i. **Precedence is now provider → observed → configured** (`resolveGrantExpiry` in shared, replacing `grantExpiry`).
- **Why upstream info alone can't work (verified in the vendored code, don't re-derive):** `workers-oauth-provider` — what Linear + Sentry run — builds its token response as `{access_token, token_type, expires_in, scope, refresh_token}` (+resource): zero occurrences of `refresh_token_expires_in`, no introspection endpoint. It holds `grant.expiresAt` and puts nothing about it on the wire. AND the MCP SDK's `OAuthTokensSchema` ends in `.strip()` (`shared/auth.js:129`), so even a provider that DOES send it never reached us. RFC 6749 never defines a refresh-token lifetime, so there is no standard field to rely on.

  OAuthProviderOptions,
  TokenExchangeCallbackOptions
} from '@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider'

import type { Env } from '../env'
import { stampTokenExchange } from './login-activity'

const NOOP_HANDLER: ExportedHandler<Env> = {

/**

 *
 * Both TTLs below are passed as `undefined` on purpose — the library then
 * writes the grant and the DCR client record to KV with NO expiration, and
 * expiry becomes ours to decide. That is the only way to get a sliding
 * session out of this library: `refreshTokenTTL` is stamped once, at the
 * authorization-code exchange, and the refresh path re-saves the same
 * absolute instant (it even refuses a `refreshTokenTTL` returned from the
 * token-exchange callback). `clientRegistrationTTL` behaves the same way
 * from the registration moment, so leaving it at its 90 d default would cap
 * the login independently — the final refresh would just fail
 * `invalid_client` instead of `invalid_grant`.
 *
 * What replaces them: `tokenExchangeCallback` stamps every exchange into
 * `oauth_grant_activity`, and the nightly `grant-idle-prune` job revokes
 * grants that have been silent for `MCP_LOGIN_IDLE_DAYS`. Instant lockout is
 * unaffected — suspend/delete still calls `revokeAllUserGrants`, and the
 * session DO re-checks user status on init.

 * `env` is optional because admin tooling builds `OAuthHelpers` from these
 * same options (see the module header) and never exchanges a token; without
 * it the callback is simply not installed.

  defaultHandler: ExportedHandler<Env> = NOOP_HANDLER,
  env?: Env
): OAuthProviderOptions<Env> {

  // our handlers carry `fetch` at the value level but their declared
  // types don't line up exactly, so the whole map is cast once.
  const apiHandlers = {

    '/sse': McpSessionDO.serveSSE('/sse', { binding: 'MCP_SESSION_DO' })
  } as OAuthProviderOptions<Env>['apiHandlers']

    apiHandlers,
    defaultHandler,
    authorizeEndpoint: '/oauth/authorize',
    tokenEndpoint: '/oauth/token',
    clientRegistrationEndpoint: '/oauth/register',

    // expiration-less. See the note above before "simplifying" these away.
    refreshTokenTTL: undefined,

content.text:
I couldn't pin down the cause yet. Nothing on the server is killing your gateway login, and the evidence that would settle it sits behind a prod read the auto-mode classifier blocked ("Production Reads").

**What I checked**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Live version (both hosts) | `6bf9e6b` (Oct 12), so sliding logins are deployed |
| Nightly idle-login cleanup job, last 12 nights | `revoked: 0` every night; it isn't logging anyone out |
| OAuth library settings (0.10.3) | No login expiry and no client-registration expiry are set, so logins slide as intended |
| Our per-refresh bookkeeping hook | Returns nothing and never throws, so it can't break a refresh |
| OAuth metadata on `mcp.yukitools.dev` | Correct issuer and token endpoint |
| Claude Desktop local logs | No help: the remote connector's token refresh runs in Anthropic's backend, not on this Mac |

One thing stands out: total logins went from 344 to 438 in 11 days, about 10 new ones a day. Logins no longer die, so that count only grows when someone signs in fresh. Someone is re-logging in daily, but I can't tell who or why without per-user rows.

**Two different things could each look like a "reconnect request":**
1. **Desktop's own prompt** on the Yuki MCP connector ("Connect" / "Reconnect"). That means the gateway login really failed.
2. **ctxlayer's own notice**, which every session's instructions now open with. This session has one: *"Expiring soon — up-sentry (2d) … renew at /app/upstreams"*. With Datadog on a 14-day cycle, Linear 25 and Sentry 30, each one warns for 3 days before its cutoff and then shows "stopped" until you renew. The assistant may be repeating that notice in every chat. That's a different fix: tone down or rate-limit the notice, not change OAuth.

**What would settle it:**
- **Which one are you seeing?** If it's #2, renewing Sentry at https://ctxlayer.yukitools.dev/app/upstreams clears today's notice.
- **If it's #1:** run a Workers Logs query for `"OAuth error response"` over the last 48h and paste the result. `Invalid refresh token` would mean a token-rotation race. `Grant not found` or `invalid_token` would mean the login itself is gone. No lines at all would mean the server never rejected you and the problem is on Desktop's side.
- **Or allow the prod D1 read**, and I'll pull your own login history (one new row a day means real daily re-logins). You can also run it yourself:
  ```
  ! /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-stevenn-Projects-satisa-ctxlayer/6f120ecf-c461-4e4a-888f-144a7d35b8c2/scratchpad/q.sh "select substr(grant_id,1,12) g, datetime(created_at,'unixepoch') created, datetime(last_refresh_at,'unixepoch') last_refresh from oauth_grant_activity where user_id like 'ba4b75d6%' order by created_at desc limit 20"
  ```
it's the Desktop connector prompt, not the notice
A Desktop prompt means the gateway refresh itself is failing. A nightly job that deletes OAuth clients would produce exactly that daily pattern, so I'm checking the client-prune job next.

content.text:
That rules out the most likely server-side cause. Nothing on our side is deleting your login or the Desktop connector's client registration. To go further I need two prod reads I can't run: the classifier blocked per-user queries.

**Ruled out (from the job ledger, last 10–12 nights)**

| Suspect | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Nightly client-registration cleanup removing Desktop's client | `deleted: 0` every night (1,183 clients scanned) |
| Nightly idle-login cleanup revoking your login | `revoked: 0` every night |
| Logins or client registrations expiring on a fixed date | Both lifetimes are unset, so they never expire |
| Our own code returning 401 on `/mcp` | It doesn't; only the OAuth library issues 401s there |
| Desktop's connector URL resolving to the wrong host | OAuth metadata on `mcp.yukitools.dev` is correct |

**What's left**
- **Refresh-token rotation race.** The library accepts only the current refresh token and the one before it. If Anthropic's backend refreshes twice at once, or retries a refresh whose reply got lost, it ends up holding a token two steps old. That gets `invalid_grant – Invalid refresh token`, and Desktop asks you to reconnect.
- **Token loss on Claude's side.** The Desktop connector's tokens live in Anthropic's backend, and we've seen a bug in hosted connectors before (the dropped-blob issue in October). If it's this, the server never rejects anything; Desktop just starts a new login.

**What would decide it** (either one is enough):
1. Workers Logs, last 48h, query `"OAuth error response"`, then paste the lines.
   - `Invalid refresh token` → rotation race. I can fix that on our side by keeping more previous refresh tokens valid for a short grace window.
   - `Grant not found` / `invalid_token` → the login is being removed, so I'd keep digging on our side.
   - Nothing around the time of your last prompt → Claude-side. File it with Anthropic; I can't fix it from here.
2. Your own login history: one new row per day confirms daily re-logins, and the last refresh time on each old row shows whether refreshing had stopped beforehand:
   ```
   ! /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-stevenn-Projects-satisa-ctxlayer/6f120ecf-c461-4e4a-888f-144a7d35b8c2/scratchpad/q.sh "select substr(grant_id,1,12) g, substr(client_id,1,10) c, datetime(created_at,'unixepoch') created, datetime(last_refresh_at,'unixepoch') last_refresh from oauth_grant_activity where user_id like 'ba4b75d6%' order by created_at desc limit 20"
   ```
   If old logins kept refreshing right up until a new one appeared, the server was still accepting them. That points to Claude-side token loss, not a rejection.

If you'd rather I run these myself, add a Bash permission rule for that script.

input.command: curl -s -i --max-time 10 -X POST https://mcp.yukitools.dev/mcp -H 'Authorization: Bearer x:y:z' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' | grep -iE "^HTTP|www-authenticate|^\{"
input.description: Check 401 response headers from MCP endpoint

content.text:
The paste rules out the server. Every line is `401 invalid_token – Invalid access token` on `POST /mcp`. There is no error from the token endpoint (`/oauth/token`) anywhere in it: no `invalid_grant`, no `Invalid refresh token`, no `invalid_client`. So in this window (Nov 5 18:27 → Nov 6 18:59 UTC, the 60 most recent lines) ctxlayer never rejected a refresh.

**What those 401s are**
- Access tokens last 1h and are stored in KV with a 1h expiry. An expired token simply no longer exists, so the library reports it as "Invalid access token", not "expired".
- A 401 like this is the normal signal to refresh. I checked the response just now and it's spec-correct: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer … resource_metadata="…/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", error="invalid_token"`.
- A healthy client refreshes on that 401 and carries on. A failed refresh would show up as a 400 on `/oauth/token`, and there isn't one.

**What this points to:** when the token expires, the Desktop connector (running in Anthropic's backend) sometimes asks you to reconnect instead of refreshing. Either it doesn't try, or the attempt never reaches us. That's on Claude's side.

**One query to confirm it:** in Workers Logs over the same 24h, filter on request path `/oauth/token` (all statuses, not just warnings).
- **Few or no requests** (well under one per active user per hour): the connector isn't refreshing at all. File it with Anthropic as "remote connector ignores the refresh token on a 401 and prompts reconnect", with a ray id from your paste (e.g. `a56655f7cf73b6c4`).
- **Plenty of 200s:** refreshes work in general and only fail in some way that never reaches us. Note the exact time of your next Desktop prompt and I'll match it against the 401s and refreshes around that minute.

**A workaround I can build either way:** raise the gateway's access-token lifetime from 1h to something like 7 days. If the connector rarely refreshes, the prompts would drop to about once per token lifetime.
- The security cost is small here. Suspending or deleting a user already deletes their tokens from KV (`revokeAllUserGrants`), and the session checks user status when it starts, so lockout stays instant.
- What we give up is a short lifetime for a leaked bearer token.
- It's a one-line change in `oauth/provider-config.ts` (`accessTokenTTL`) plus a test. Want me to do it?

content.text:
Every refresh in those logs succeeded. The likely cause is that Claude's hosted connector doesn't refresh when its token expires mid-use; it shows you the Reconnect prompt instead, and your click is what refreshes it.

**Who's calling `/oauth/token`** (Nov 5 19:20 → Nov 8 16:26 UTC, every call returned 200)

| Client | User agent / origin | Request body size | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude's hosted connector (Desktop / claude.ai) | `python-httpx/0.28.1`, Anthropic IPs in Columbus OH | 246 bytes, once 450 | 246 = refresh. 450 = a full new login, and there's only one (Nov 7 11:35) in ~3 days |
| Claude Code | `Bun/1.4.4`, EU home IPs | 199 bytes | Ordinary refreshes |

**The timing pattern**

Matching your first paste against this one, the hosted connector's refreshes come right after a run of 401s:

| `/mcp` returns 401 | Next hosted-connector refresh |
|---|---|
| 12:09, 12:19, 12:43, 12:55, 13:00, 13:05, 13:09:16 | 13:09:28 |
| 14:55:23 | 14:56:09 |
| 18:16:16 | 18:18:00 |
| 08:35:10 | 08:39:52 |

So when the 1-hour access token expires and the connector gets a 401, it doesn't refresh. It leaves the token dead until a person acts; a 401 run lasting a full hour (12:09 → 13:09) only fits that. When you click Reconnect, it does a normal refresh-token exchange, which we accept. That's why there are no new logins and no rejections.

One caveat: the 401 lines don't include a user agent, so I matched them to the hosted connector by timing alone. Adding user agent to that query would make it airtight.

**Nothing in ctxlayer is broken**, but there are two things to do:
1. **Workaround on our side:** make access tokens last longer, so the connector runs into an expired token roughly once per token lifetime instead of after every hour-long gap. I'd use 7 days. 24 hours would still prompt you daily, and 30 days would mean a leaked token stays usable that long. Lockout stays instant: suspending or deleting a user still wipes their tokens, and each request re-checks user status. Logins still slide. 7 days is well under the 90-day idle cutoff, so an active connector never trips it. It's one line in `oauth/provider-config.ts` (`accessTokenTTL`), a test pinning it, and `bun run verify`. Nothing gets committed or deployed until you say so.
2. **Report it to Anthropic:** "remote MCP connector gets 401 `invalid_token` (with a correct `WWW-Authenticate` header) and prompts to reconnect instead of using its refresh token; the reconnect then succeeds via `refresh_token`." Ray-id pair as evidence: 401 `a56454e72aa3f368` → refresh `a564552e9fe796a2`.

Shall I make the 7-day change, or would you rather pick a different lifetime?

I saved this diagnosis to memory, so the server-side OAuth path doesn't get re-investigated for this symptom.
